verses.original: וְדָוִ֗ד עָבַ֤ר מְעַט֙ מֵֽהָרֹ֔אשׁ וְהִנֵּ֥ה צִיבָ֛א נַ֥עַר מְפִי־ בֹ֖שֶׁת לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וְצֶ֨מֶד חֲמֹרִ֜ים חֲבֻשִׁ֗ים וַעֲלֵיהֶם֩ מָאתַ֨יִם לֶ֜חֶם וּמֵאָ֧ה צִמּוּקִ֛ים וּמֵ֥אָה קַ֖יִץ וְנֵ֥בֶל יָֽיִן׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḏā·wiḏ ‘ā·ḇar mə·‘aṭ mê·hā·rōš wə·hin·nêh ṣî·ḇā na·‘ar mə·p̄î- ḇō·šeṯ liq·rā·ṯōw wə·ṣe·meḏ ḥă·mō·rîm ḥă·ḇu·šîm wa·‘ă·lê·hem mā·ṯa·yim le·ḥem ū·mê·’āh ṣim·mū·qîm ū·mê·’āh qa·yiṣ wə·nê·ḇel yā·yin
verses.literal: When David had gone a little beyond the summit Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him He had a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread a hundred clusters of raisins a hundred summer fruits and a skin of wine
verses.literalPt: E PASSANDO Davi um pouco mais adiante do cume, eis que Ziba, o servo de Mefibosete, veio encontrar-se com ele, com um par de jumentos albardados, e sobre eles duzentos pães, com cem cachos de passas, e cem de frutas de verão e um odre de vinho.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־ צִיבָ֖א מָה־ אֵ֣לֶּה לָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר צִ֠יבָא הַחֲמוֹרִ֨ים לְבֵית־ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לִרְכֹּ֗ב וּלְהַלֶּחֶם וְהַקַּ֙יִץ֙ לֶאֱכ֣וֹל הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְהַיַּ֕יִן לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת הַיָּעֵ֖ף בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’el- ṣî·ḇā māh- ’êl·leh lāḵ way·yō·mer ṣî·ḇā ha·ḥă·mō·w·rîm lə·ḇêṯ- ham·me·leḵ lir·kōḇ ū·lə·hal·lɛ·ḥɛm wə·haq·qa·yiṣ le·’ĕ·ḵō·wl han·nə·‘ā·rîm wə·hay·ya·yin liš·tō·wṯ hay·yā·‘êp̄ bam·miḏ·bār
verses.literal: Why do you have these asked the king - Ziba replied The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness
verses.literalPt: E disse o rei a Ziba: Que pretendes com isto? E disse Ziba: Os jumentos são para a casa do rei, para se montarem neles; e o pão e as frutas de verão para comerem os moços; e o vinho para beberem os cansados no deserto.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאַיֵּ֖ה בֶּן־ אֲדֹנֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר צִיבָ֜א אֶל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הִנֵּה֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר הַיּ֗וֹם יָשִׁ֤יבוּ לִי֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת מַמְלְכ֥וּת אָבִֽי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ wə·’ay·yêh ben- ’ă·ḏō·ne·ḵā way·yō·mer ṣî·ḇā ’el- ham·me·leḵ hin·nêh yō·wō·šêḇ bî·rū·šā·lim kî ’ā·mar hay·yō·wm yā·šî·ḇū lî bêṯ yiś·rā·’êl ’êṯ mam·lə·ḵūṯ ’ā·ḇî
verses.literal: Where is your master’s grandson asked the king And Ziba answered - Indeed he is staying in Jerusalem for he has said Today the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather
verses.literalPt: Então disse o rei: Ora, onde está o filho de teu senhor? E disse Ziba ao rei: Eis que ficou em Jerusalém; porque disse: Hoje me restituirá a casa de Israel o reino de meu pai.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לְצִבָ֔א הִנֵּ֣ה לְךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִמְפִי־ בֹ֑שֶׁת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ הִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֵ֔יתִי אֶמְצָא־ חֵ֥ן בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ lə·ṣi·ḇā hin·nêh lə·ḵā kōl ’ă·šer lim·p̄î- ḇō·šeṯ way·yō·mer ṣî·ḇā hiš·ta·ḥă·wê·ṯî ’em·ṣā- ḥên bə·‘ê·ne·ḵā ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: So the king said to Ziba All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours I humbly bow before you said Ziba May I find favor in your eyes my lord the king
verses.literalPt: Então disse o rei a Ziba: Eis que teu é tudo quanto tem Mefibosete. E disse Ziba: Eu me inclino, que eu ache graça em teus olhos, ó rei meu senhor.

verses.original: וּבָ֛א הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִ֖ד עַד־ בַּֽחוּרִ֑ים וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשָּׁם֩ אִ֨ישׁ יוֹצֵ֜א מִמִּשְׁפַּ֣חַת בֵּית־ שָׁא֗וּל וּשְׁמוֹ֙ שִׁמְעִ֣י בֶן־ גֵּרָ֔א יֹצֵ֥א יָצ֖וֹא וּמְקַלֵּֽל׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḇā ham·me·leḵ dā·wiḏ ‘aḏ- ba·ḥū·rîm wə·hin·nêh miš·šām ’îš yō·w·ṣê mim·miš·pa·ḥaṯ bêṯ- šā·’ūl ū·šə·mōw šim·‘î ḇen- gê·rā yō·ṣê yā·ṣō·w ū·mə·qal·lêl
verses.literal: As King David approached . . . Bahurim a man from the family of the house of Saul was just . . . coming out His name was Shimei son of Gera and as he approached . . . he kept yelling out curses
verses.literalPt: E, chegando o rei Davi a Baurim, eis que dali saiu um homem da linhagem da casa de Saul, cujo nome era Simei, filho de Gera, e, saindo, ia amaldiçoando.

verses.original: וַיְסַקֵּ֤ל בָּֽאֲבָנִים֙ אֶת־ דָּוִ֔ד וְאֶת־ כָּל־ עַבְדֵ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ וְכָל־ הַגִּבֹּרִ֔ים מִימִינ֖וֹ וּמִשְּׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·saq·qêl bā·’ă·ḇā·nîm ’eṯ- dā·wiḏ wə·’eṯ- kāl- ‘aḇ·ḏê ham·me·leḵ dā·wiḏ wə·ḵāl hā·‘ām wə·ḵāl hag·gib·bō·rîm mî·mî·nōw ū·miś·śə·mō·lōw
verses.literal: He threw stones . . . at David and at all the servants of the king though the troops and all the mighty men were on David’s . . . right and left
verses.literalPt: E atirava pedras contra Davi, e contra todos os servos do rei Davi; ainda que todo o povo e todos os valentes iam à sua direita e à sua esquerda.

verses.original: וְכֹֽה־ אָמַ֥ר שִׁמְעִ֖י בְּקַֽלְל֑וֹ צֵ֥א צֵ֛א אִ֥ישׁ הַדָּמִ֖ים וְאִ֥ישׁ הַבְּלִיָּֽעַל׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḵōh- ’ā·mar šim·‘î bə·qal·lōw ṣê ṣê ’îš had·dā·mîm wə·’îš hab·bə·lî·yā·‘al
verses.literal: And as he yelled curses Shimei said Get out get out you worthless man of bloodshed . . .
verses.literalPt: E, amaldiçoando-o Simei, assim dizia: Sai, sai, homem de sangue, e homem de Belial.

verses.original: הֵשִׁיב֩ עָלֶ֨יךָ יְהוָ֜ה כֹּ֣ל׀ דְּמֵ֣י בֵית־ שָׁא֗וּל אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָלַ֙כְתָּ֙ תַּחְתּוֹ וַיִּתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בְּנֶ֑ךָ וְהִנְּךָ֙ בְּרָ֣עָתֶ֔ךָ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ דָּמִ֖ים אָֽתָּה׃
verses.transliteration: hê·šîḇ ‘ā·le·ḵā Yah·weh kōl də·mê ḇêṯ- šā·’ūl ’ă·šer mā·laḵ·tā taḥ·tō way·yit·tên Yah·weh ’eṯ- ham·mə·lū·ḵāh bə·yaḏ ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm bə·ne·ḵā wə·hin·nə·ḵā bə·rā·‘ā·ṯe·ḵā kî ’îš dā·mîm ’āt·tāh
verses.literal: The LORD has paid you back . . . for all the blood of the house of Saul in whose place you have reigned and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom See you have come to ruin because you are a man of bloodshed
verses.literalPt: O SENHOR te deu agora a paga de todo o sangue da casa de Saul, em cujo lugar tens reinado; já deu o SENHOR o reino na mão de Absalão teu filho; e eis-te agora na tua desgraça, porque és um homem de sangue.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן־ צְרוּיָה֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֣מָּה יְקַלֵּ֞ל הַכֶּ֤לֶב הַמֵּת֙ הַזֶּ֔ה אֶת־ אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ אֶעְבְּרָה־ נָּ֖א וְאָסִ֥ירָה אֶת־ רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ă·ḇî·šay ben- ṣə·rū·yāh ’el- ham·me·leḵ lām·māh yə·qal·lêl hak·ke·leḇ ham·mêṯ haz·zeh ’eṯ- ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ ’e‘·bə·rāh- nā wə·’ā·sî·rāh ’eṯ- rō·šōw
verses.literal: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king Let me go over . . . and cut off his head . . .
verses.literalPt: Então disse Abisai, filho de Zeruia, ao rei: Por que amaldiçoaria este cão morto ao rei meu senhor? Deixa-me passar, e lhe tirarei a cabeça.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מַה־ לִּ֥י וְלָכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י צְרֻיָ֑ה כִּי יְקַלֵּ֗ל וְכִי יְהוָה֙ אָ֤מַר לוֹ֙ קַלֵּ֣ל אֶת־ דָּוִ֔ד וּמִ֣י יֹאמַ֔ר מַדּ֖וּעַ עָשִׂ֥יתָה כֵּֽן׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ mah- lî wə·lā·ḵem bə·nê ṣə·ru·yāh kī yə·qal·lêl wə·ḵī Yah·weh ’ā·mar lōw qal·lêl ’eṯ- dā·wiḏ ū·mî yō·mar mad·dū·a‘ ‘ā·śî·ṯāh kên
verses.literal: But the king replied What have I to do with you O sons of Zeruiah If he curses me because the LORD told him Curse David who can ask Why did you do this
verses.literalPt: Disse, porém, o rei: Que tenho eu convosco, filhos de Zeruia? Ora deixai-o amaldiçoar; pois o SENHOR lhe disse: Amaldiçoa a Davi; quem pois diria: Por que assim fizeste?

verses.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤ד אֶל־ אֲבִישַׁי֙ וְאֶל־ כָּל־ עֲבָדָ֔יו הִנֵּ֥ה בְנִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־ יָצָ֥א מִמֵּעַ֖י מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֶת־ נַפְשִׁ֑י וְאַ֨ף כִּֽי־ עַתָּ֜ה בֶּן־ הַיְמִינִ֗י הַנִּ֤חוּ לוֹ֙ וִֽיקַלֵּ֔ל כִּ֥י אָֽמַר־ ל֖וֹ יְהוָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer dā·wiḏ ’el- ’ă·ḇî·šay wə·’el- kāl- ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw hin·nêh ḇə·nî ’ă·šer- yā·ṣā mim·mê·‘ay mə·ḇaq·qêš ’eṯ- nap̄·šî wə·’ap̄ kî- ‘at·tāh ben- hay·mî·nî han·ni·ḥū lōw wî·qal·lêl kî ’ā·mar- lōw Yah·weh
verses.literal: Then David said to Abishai . . . and to all his servants Behold my own son - my own flesh and blood seeks my life How much more then this Benjamite Leave him alone . . . and let him curse me for the LORD has told him so
verses.literalPt: Disse mais Davi a Abisai, e a todos os seus servos: Eis que meu filho, que saiu das minhas entranhas, procura a minha morte; quanto mais ainda este benjamita? Deixai-o, que amaldiçoe; porque o SENHOR lho disse.

verses.original: אוּלַ֛י יִרְאֶ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה בְּעֲוֹנִי וְהֵשִׁ֨יב יְהוָ֥ה לִי֙ טוֹבָ֔ה תַּ֥חַת קִלְלָת֖וֹ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: ’ū·lay yir·’eh Yah·weh bə·ʿă·wō·nī wə·hê·šîḇ Yah·weh lî ṭō·w·ḇāh ta·ḥaṯ qil·lā·ṯōw hay·yō·wm haz·zeh
verses.literal: Perhaps the LORD will see my affliction and repay . . . me with good for the cursing I receive today . . .
verses.literalPt: Porventura o SENHOR olhará para a minha miséria; e o SENHOR me pagará com bem a sua maldição deste dia.

verses.original: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ דָּוִ֛ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֖יו בַּדָּ֑רֶךְס וְשִׁמְעִ֡י הֹלֵךְ֩ בְּצֵ֨לַע הָהָ֜ר לְעֻמָּת֗וֹ הָלוֹךְ֙ וַיְקַלֵּ֔ל וַיְסַקֵּ֤ל בָּֽאֲבָנִים֙ לְעֻמָּת֔וֹ וְעִפַּ֖ר בֶּעָפָֽר׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·yê·leḵ dā·wiḏ wa·’ă·nā·šāw bad·då̄·rɛḵs wə·šim·‘î hō·lêḵ bə·ṣê·la‘ hā·hār lə·‘um·mā·ṯōw hā·lō·wḵ way·qal·lêl way·saq·qêl bā·’ă·ḇā·nîm lə·‘um·mā·ṯōw wə·‘ip·par be·‘ā·p̄ār
verses.literal: So David and his men proceeded along the road as Shimei went along the ridge of the hill opposite him As Shimei went he yelled curses threw stones . . . and flung dust at David
verses.literalPt: Prosseguiram, pois, o seu caminho, Davi e os seus homens; e também Simei ia ao longo do monte, defronte dele, caminhando e amaldiçoando, e atirava pedras contra ele, e levantava poeira.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָל־ הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֖וֹ עֲיֵפִ֑ים וַיִּנָּפֵ֖שׁ שָֽׁם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō ham·me·leḵ wə·ḵāl hā·‘ām ’ă·šer- ’it·tōw ‘ă·yê·p̄îm way·yin·nā·p̄êš šām
verses.literal: Finally, the king and all the people with him arrived exhausted And there he refreshed himself
verses.literalPt: E o rei e todo o povo que ia com ele chegaram cansados, e refrescaram-se ali.

verses.original: וְאַבְשָׁל֗וֹם וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֖אוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַאֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל אִתּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm wə·ḵāl hā·‘ām ’îš yiś·rā·’êl bā·’ū yə·rū·šā·lim wa·’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el ’it·tōw
verses.literal: Then Absalom and all . . . the men of Israel came to Jerusalem and Ahithophel was with him
verses.literalPt: Absalão, pois, e todo o povo, os homens de Israel, vieram a Jerusalém; e Aitofel com ele.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֞א חוּשַׁ֧י הָאַרְכִּ֛י רֵעֶ֥ה דָוִ֖ד אֶל־ אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר חוּשַׁי֙ אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם יְחִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî ka·’ă·šer- bā ḥū·šay hā·’ar·kî rê·‘eh ḏā·wiḏ ’el- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm way·yō·mer ḥū·šay ’el- ’aḇ·šā·lōm yə·ḥî ham·me·leḵ yə·ḥî ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: And David’s friend Hushai the Archite went to Absalom and said to him Long live the king Long live the king
verses.literalPt: E sucedeu que, chegando Husai, o arquita, amigo de Davi, a Absalão, disse Husai a Absalão: Viva o rei, viva o rei!

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־ חוּשַׁ֔י זֶ֥ה חַסְדְּךָ֖ אֶת־ רֵעֶ֑ךָ לָ֥מָּה לֹֽא־ הָלַ֖כְתָּ אֶת־ רֵעֶֽךָ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’el- ḥū·šay zeh ḥas·də·ḵā ’eṯ- rê·‘e·ḵā lām·māh lō- hā·laḵ·tā ’eṯ- rê·‘e·ḵā
verses.literal: Is this the loyalty you show your friend Absalom replied . . . . . . Why did you not go with your friend
verses.literalPt: Porém Absalão disse a Husai: É esta a tua beneficência para com o teu amigo? Por que não foste com o teu amigo?

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁי֮ אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלֹם֒ לֹ֕א כִּי֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּחַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה וְהָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה וְכָל־ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹא אֶהְיֶ֖ה וְאִתּ֥וֹ אֵשֵֽׁב׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ḥū·šay ’el- ’aḇ·šā·lōm lō kî ’ă·šer bā·ḥar Yah·weh wə·hā·‘ām haz·zeh wə·ḵāl ’îš yiś·rā·’êl lō ’eh·yeh wə·’it·tōw ’ê·šêḇ
verses.literal: Not at all Hushai . . . answered For the one chosen by the LORD by this people and by all the men of Israel his I will be and with him I will remain
verses.literalPt: E disse Husai a Absalão: Não, porém daquele que eleger o SENHOR, e todo este povo, e todos os homens de Israel, dele serei e com ele ficarei.

verses.original: וְהַשֵּׁנִ֗ית לְמִי֙ אֲנִ֣י אֶֽעֱבֹ֔ד הֲל֖וֹא לִפְנֵ֣י בְנ֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָבַ֙דְתִּי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ כֵּ֖ן אֶהְיֶ֥ה לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃פ
verses.transliteration: wə·haš·šê·nîṯ lə·mî ’ă·nî ’e·‘ĕ·ḇōḏ hă·lō·w lip̄·nê ḇə·nōw ka·’ă·šer ‘ā·ḇaḏ·tî lip̄·nê ’ā·ḇî·ḵā kên ’eh·yeh li·p̄ā·ne·ḵā
verses.literal: Furthermore whom should I serve if not his son As I served in your father’s presence so also I will serve . . . in yours
verses.literalPt: E, demais disto, a quem serviria eu? Porventura não seria diante de seu filho? Como servi diante de teu pai, assim serei diante de ti.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל־ אֲחִיתֹ֑פֶל הָב֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם עֵצָ֖ה מַֽה־ נַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’el- ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el hā·ḇū lā·ḵem ‘ê·ṣāh mah- na·‘ă·śeh
verses.literal: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel Give me counsel What should we do
verses.literalPt: Então disse Absalão a Aitofel: Dai conselho entre vós sobre o que devemos fazer.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲחִיתֹ֙פֶל֙ אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם בּ֚וֹא אֶל־ פִּלַגְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִנִּ֖יחַ לִשְׁמ֣וֹר הַבָּ֑יִת וְשָׁמַ֤ע כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּֽי־ נִבְאַ֣שְׁתָּ אֶת־ אָבִ֔יךָ וְחָ֣זְק֔וּ יְדֵ֖י כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתָּֽךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el ’el- ’aḇ·šā·lōm bō·w ’el- pi·laḡ·šê ’ā·ḇî·ḵā ’ă·šer hin·nî·aḥ liš·mō·wr hab·bā·yiṯ wə·šā·ma‘ kāl- yiś·rā·’êl kî- niḇ·’aš·tā ’eṯ- ’ā·ḇî·ḵā wə·ḥā·zə·qū yə·ḏê kāl- ’ă·šer ’it·tāḵ
verses.literal: Ahithophel replied - Sleep with . . . your father’s concubines whom he has left to take care of the palace When all Israel hears that you have become a stench to your father then the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened
verses.literalPt: E disse Aitofel a Absalão: Possue as concubinas de teu pai, que deixou para guardarem a casa; e assim todo o Israel ouvirá que te fizeste aborrecível para com teu pai; e se fortalecerão as mãos de todos os que estão contigo.

verses.original: וַיַּטּ֧וּ לְאַבְשָׁל֛וֹם הָאֹ֖הֶל עַל־ הַגָּ֑ג וַיָּבֹ֤א אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־ פִּֽלַגְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֔יו לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
verses.transliteration: way·yaṭ·ṭū lə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm hā·’ō·hel ‘al- hag·gāḡ way·yā·ḇō ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’el- pi·laḡ·šê ’ā·ḇîw lə·‘ê·nê kāl- yiś·rā·’êl
verses.literal: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof and he slept with . . . his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel
verses.literalPt: Estenderam, pois, para Absalão uma tenda no terraço; e Absalão possuiu as concubinas de seu pai, perante os olhos de todo o Israel.

verses.original: וַעֲצַ֣ת אֲחִיתֹ֗פֶל אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָעַץ֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשְׁאַלִ֖־ בִּדְבַ֣ר הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כֵּ֚ן כָּל־ עֲצַ֣ת אֲחִיתֹ֔פֶל גַּם־ לְדָוִ֖ד גַּ֥ם לְאַבְשָׁלֹֽם׃ס
verses.transliteration: wa·‘ă·ṣaṯ ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el ’ă·šer yā·‘aṣ bay·yā·mîm hā·hêm ka·’ă·šer yiš·ʾa·li- biḏ·ḇar hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm kên kāl- ‘ă·ṣaṯ ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el gam- lə·ḏā·wiḏ gam lə·’aḇ·šā·lōm
verses.literal: Now in those days the advice of Ahithophel - was like the consultation of the word of God Such was the regard that both David and Absalom had for Ahithophel’s advice
verses.literalPt: E era o conselho de Aitofel, que aconselhava naqueles dias, como se a palavra de Deus se consultara; tal era todo o conselho de Aitofel, assim para com Davi como para com Absalão.
